headline: Per-request deadline translation does not guarantee graceful degradation under overload.
claim: Fine-grained QoS classes and deadline translation alone do not guarantee graceful service degradation when load exceeds capacity; QoServe needs hybrid prioritization and eager relegation to avoid cascading violations.
paper_fact: EDF which prioritizes requests with earlier deadline has very low deadline violation rates (Figure 2(c)) at low loads, but the violation rates spike to almost 100% once the load exceeds a certain threshold.
premise: Deadline-aware scheduling is not overload control; queue buildup and head-of-line blocking can cause cascading misses even when deadlines are computed per request.
inference: Since the paper reports EDF collapses at high load and states QoServe or any policy cannot service all requests at desired SLOs under overload, deadline translation alone cannot guarantee graceful degradation; the guarantee depends on additional mechanisms and capacity assumptions.
toy_example: Not a measurement: an EDF queue receives many requests with near deadlines while one long prefill occupies the batch; later requests miss deadlines despite having computed deadlines.
conditional_consequence: If load exceeds capacity and no relegation or hybrid prioritization is active, per-request deadlines may produce cascading violations rather than graceful degradation.
critical_link: The link is that deadlines order work but do not create capacity; overload behavior is determined by queue management, preemption, and relegation, not by deadline translation alone.
necessary_conditions: Load is within or near capacity
Application priority hints are available for multi-tenant relegation
defeaters: Paper reports QoServe reduces SLO violations by an order of magnitude under extreme load
Paper reports relegating 5% maintains latency SLOs under high overload
Paper reports QoServe misses no important tasks in transient overload
do_not_infer: Do not infer that QoServe fails under overload
Do not infer that deadline translation is useless
Author boundary: the paper does not claim deadline translation alone guarantees graceful degradation

headline: Deadline-slack dynamic chunking does not guarantee throughput gains under PD disaggregation with a large default prefill chunk.
claim: QoServe's dynamic chunking is not exploited in PD disaggregation when the default prefill chunk is already large, so disaggregated throughput results cannot be used as evidence for the chunking mechanism's benefit.
paper_fact: The throughput gains are lower compared to PD colocation because we are unable to exploit dynamic chunking here, because of the large baseline chunk size.
premise: Dynamic chunking can increase chunk size only if the current/default chunk size is below the maximum useful chunk and if latency slack exists; if the baseline already uses a large chunk, there is little or no headroom for slack-based growth.
inference: A PD-disaggregated artifact run may show smaller gains than the colocated 20% dynamic-chunking result, and those gains should not be attributed to dynamic chunking unless the baseline chunk size and TBT constraints are changed.
toy_example: Toy example (not a measurement): if the baseline prefill chunk is already 8K and the policy has no TBT constraint forcing a smaller chunk, slack-based chunk maximization has no lever to increase throughput.
conditional_consequence: If the artifact evaluates PD disaggregation with an 8K default prefill chunk, then dynamic chunking should not be expected to reproduce the colocated chunking gain; any observed gain should be attributed to other mechanisms or to a different baseline.
critical_link: The critical link is baseline chunk-size headroom plus a latency budget that constrains chunk size; without those, deadline slack cannot be converted into larger chunks.
necessary_conditions: PD colocation or a small default prefill chunk
TBT or another latency budget that constrains chunk size
a predictor that maps batch statistics to latency
defeaters: baseline chunk size is reduced below the maximum useful chunk
dynamic chunking is applied to a different phase or deployment mode
the artifact uses a different maximum chunk size
do_not_infer: Do not infer that dynamic chunking is ineffective in general; the authors only report that it is not exploited in PD disaggregation with a large baseline chunk.
Do not infer that PD-disaggregation gains are due to dynamic chunking.
Do not infer artifact failure from lower disaggregated gains alone.
lens: deployment mode and baseline chunk-size headroom

headline: Artifact coverage of Llama3-8B TP1 on Azure Code does not imply reproduction of the paper's cross-model and cross-trace generality.
claim: The artifact's reported reproduction scope does not guarantee reproduction of the paper's goodput gains across Qwen-7B, Llama3-70B, ShareGPT, or all PD configurations.
paper_fact: Current artifact reproduces Llama3-8B TP1 on Azure Code Trace.
premise: A reproduction artifact that covers one model/hardware/trace combination is not evidence that other model/hardware/trace combinations in the paper were reproduced.
inference: The artifact supports a narrow reproduction claim, not the paper's full generality claim; cross-model/hardware/trace results remain paper-reported and not artifact-verified.
toy_example: Toy example, not a measurement: reproducing one Llama3-8B/A100/Azure-Code point is like checking one cell of a table; it does not fill the other cells.
conditional_consequence: If artifact reviewers require cross-model reproduction, this artifact alone is insufficient; if they accept trend-level single-model reproduction, it may be sufficient for that narrower claim.
critical_link: The link is the mapping between artifact scripts and paper figures: fig7.sh and fig8.sh are limited to Llama3-8B TP1, while paper Figure 7 spans three models and three datasets.
necessary_conditions: Artifact must run the same model/hardware/trace combinations as paper
Artifact must use comparable request volumes and QPS sweep
Artifact must reproduce both colocated and disaggregated configurations
defeaters: Artifact includes additional scripts or results for Qwen-7B, Llama3-70B, ShareGPT, or full QPS sweep
Paper's generality claim is explicitly limited to Llama3-8B TP1
Artifact's reduced setup is shown to preserve all reported numerical results
do_not_infer: Do not infer the artifact fails to reproduce the paper's single-model trend
Do not infer the paper's cross-model results are false
Do not infer authors claim full artifact coverage
author_boundaries: Authors report artifact reproduces Llama3-8B TP1 on Azure Code and Azure Conv only
Authors note reduced requests and coarser QPS sweep may cause numerical variation
inferred_consequences: Cross-model and cross-trace generality is not artifact-verified
Artifact-based reproduction claims should be scoped to the reported model/trace
